claim: On host macos-m5pro-20260924 (Apple M5 Pro, 18 cores, 24 GB unified memory, macOS arm64), worktrunk 0.79.0 (wt, the catalog pin) ran a full worktree lifecycle in a throwaway one-commit git repository created under $TMPDIR. wt switch --create wt-probe created the branch and a sibling worktree, and wt list showed both worktrees. wt remove --foreground wt-probe then removed the worktree and deleted the branch (same commit as main). A second wt list, git worktree list, git branch --list and a directory listing showed only the main worktree left, and the probe directory was then deleted (all commands exit 0). worktrunk is installed at ~/.local/bin/wt (command -v wt) and pinned outside this repository: the host control plane's manifest.json, cited by its repository-relative path, pins worktrunk 0.79.0, which matches wt --version (both in the first two commands' output).
limitations: Hooks were inspected before any wt command ran. wt config show and the file system found no worktrunk user config (~/.config/worktrunk/config.toml absent), so there were no user hooks, no approvals file, and the default worktree-path template applied. There was also no system config, no WORKTRUNK_* or XDG_CONFIG_* override, and no project .config/wt.toml in the throwaway repository or in this repository. Every wt lifecycle command ran with stdin from /dev/null and without --yes or --no-hooks, so a hook approval prompt would have failed closed; none appeared. worktrunk's Claude Code plugin registers only Claude Code event hooks (status markers and Claude's own WorktreeCreate/WorktreeRemove), which a wt CLI run does not trigger.

Scope: one create/list/remove cycle of a branch at the same commit as main, in a repository with no remote. wt ran from a non-interactive /bin/sh without active shell integration, so wt switch created the worktree but could not change the calling shell's directory, as its output says. wt remove ran with --foreground so that the next wt list saw the finished removal. Not exercised: the default background removal, wt merge, hooks, generated commit messages, CI-status columns and remote branches.

The first command reads the pin from the control plane's manifest.json through CONTROL_PLANE_ROOT, an environment variable holding that private repository's root; the root path is not recorded. The throwaway repository's one commit used a fixed probe identity, commit.gpgsign=false and core.hooksPath=/dev/null, so the host's global git hooks and commit signing did not touch that setup commit. The wt commands ran with the host's normal git configuration. TMPDIR pointed at this session's temporary directory. A dry run of the same sequence just before this recording created no worktrunk state directory under the home directory and left the global git config files unmodified.
